Connect to Databricks

spark_connect_databricks.Rd

spark_connect_databricks() opens a Spark Connect session on a Databricks workspace: on serverless compute by default, or on a cluster given by its id. It is spark_connect() with the connection string and the header Databricks needs to choose the compute: for serverless, an x-databricks-session-id header carrying the session id; for a cluster, an x-databricks-cluster-id header. The cluster must be running.

Usage

spark_connect_databricks(
  host = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_HOST"),
  token = Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_TOKEN"),
  cluster_id = NULL,
  ...,
  session_id = NULL,
  headers = NULL
)

Arguments

host

The workspace URL, such as "https://dbc-1a2b3c4d-5e6f.cloud.databricks.com", with or without https://. It defaults to the DATABRICKS_HOST environment variable.

token

A personal access token. It defaults to the DATABRICKS_TOKEN environment variable.

cluster_id

NULL for serverless compute, or the id of a cluster.

...

Passed on to spark_connect(): user_id, user_agent, deadline, or more connection string parameters.

session_id

The session's id, a UUID; by default a new version 4 UUID. On serverless compute it is also sent as x-databricks-session-id.

headers

Extra headers for every call, as a named character vector, for names that are not valid in a URL.

Value

A zuspark_connection.

See also

The Connect to Databricks article.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # nzchar(Sys.getenv("DATABRICKS_TOKEN"))
con <- spark_connect_databricks()
spark_version(con)
spark_disconnect(con)
}
